name: Azca
description:
Once a fierce seafaring people feared the world over, the Dwarves of Azca met their match when they provoked the Red Dragon Flight, beginning a long and bloody conflict which, strangely enough, ended in an alliance between the Dwarves and the Dragons.

Their mutual love of riches and finely crafted treasures being amplified in each other’s presence, the resultant civilization turned greedily inward, hungrily forging the region’s natural resources into craftings for their ever-growing hordes.

Whether it was the presence of the Dragons or the deep delving of the Dwarves, the land broke and belched forth its riches from innumerable cracks and crevices amid the steaming jungle hills. The Azcans seized these fiery rivers, channeling them into canals that ran through their growing towns and cities to fuel their massive ceremonial forges.

Today, the residents of the ancient Dwarven realm bear little resemblance to the bloodthirsty, seafaring conquerors of centuries past, and the Dragons are nowhere to be seen (though Dragonborn of Dwarven stature abound). Life in Azca is centered around highly ritualized traditions of forge work and the solemn deposit of these works into the Royal Hoards, which are never seen except by members of the Royal Family and the highest-ranking members of the Priesthood.

That solemnity, however, is daily broken more and more by an influx of pleasure-seekers, who come to visit or - increasingly - to stay among the beautiful, lush lagoons, the shady groves laden with fruit, the luxuriant hot springs, and the ever-so-charming locals, who keep up their ever-so-charming traditions.

But even as these newcomers bring with them a love of peace and pleasure, they also bring rumor of the great wealth of other nations - rumor which no doubt reaches the ears of those who remember days of glory. The Great Mountain has become restless, and there are those who whisper that the Red Dragon Flight is not gone from this world...

hooks.name: Lava Pearls
hooks.description:
Legend has it that the deepest chambers of the Great Mountain contain deposits of "lava pearls" - highly prized, small, white, rounded gemstones that form on the walls of magma chambers. The most ancient and venerated Azcan works of craft feature them prominently, but none have been harvested for centuries.

Bolonoc, a young acolyte-smith in the Royal Forges, wants to prove himself capable of great works, and is determined to enter the depths of the mountain to find lava pearls. They are paying top dollar for a party of escorts to haul gear and provide protection.
hooks.gmNotes:
This fetch quest can start out innocently enough: challenging terrain to traverse, fiery beings to battle on the way into the heart of the mountain, etc.

At least once, though, there should be hints at something more: a rock wall that seems to suddenly lift and fly off into the darkness, a rumbling that sounds more like a roar, or similar.

Deep in the mountain, Our Heroes discover a chamber quite literally piled with lava pearls, but soon learn that it is in fact part of a massive hoard guarded by dozens of giant, sleeping dragons: the Ancient Red Dragon Flight.

From here you could have just one of the dragons wake and give battle. Or perhaps a young dragon is given the task of dispatching the intruders - and thus on one side we have the dragon looking to prove itself, and on the other we have Bolonoc looking to prove themselves. Azca became what it was through an unlikely alliance. Will Our Heroes attempt another? Or will it just be a good old-fashioned dragon battle?

Alternately, you might consider something darker: Perhaps Bolonoc has in fact been sent by the High Priests of the Royal Forge to deliver an offering to the Red Dragon Flight to request that they emerge to wield their great power for Azca once more. What sort of offering could be worth such might? Well, a party of adventurers hired under false pretenses might be a good start...

hooks.name: The Golden Flower
hooks.description:
A piece of Azca's history as fierce, marauding seafarers lives on in the cave harbors. The Altaxochi ("Golden Flower"), flagship of the ancient fleet, has been carefully maintained year after year, so that it may be brought out for an annual heritage festival at the end of the rainy season.

While the most prominent places on the deck will be taken up by local nobility, the Royal Navy is looking to hire ship hands for the day, and word has it that they would prefer to hire foreigners: very unusual for a Navy that is largely a ceremonial organization in these days of peace.
hooks.gmNotes:
The ship is an impressive sight: every inch of it painted red, black and gold, its rails and rigging hung with garlands of flowers, its sails woven with elaborate depictions of its exploits. It will be the centerpiece of the festival.

Our Heroes should find themselves alongside a rough crowd of other hired foreigners - ruffians of the lowest order who seem barely able to tie a rigging. The ensigns charged with training them all seem indifferent to the quality of work, and Our Heroes should catch sight of the Fleet Admiral, who is newly appointed to the position and who was already famous as a warmongering courtier who has the Monarch's ear.

It was by this Admiral's orders that a crew of foreigners was hired. They want Azca to retake its place as a world power and, having failed to convince the Monarch with words, they intend to resort to violence. Specifically, they're going to blow up the Altaxochi and frame the foreigners on board.

Whether and how Our Heroes should learn of this is up to you, as are the Admiral's specific methods: way too many fireworks in the hold, a sabotaged rigging that will cause a crash, etc. Perhaps Our Heroes are given uniforms that include some detail that will later be used against them, identifying them as members of some violent foreign group - real or invented.

The crux of the adventure could be attempting to stop things before they happen and/or dealing with the aftermath, possibly in the custody of the Admiral.

hooks.name: The Court Botanist
hooks.description: The court botanist of the Royal House is planning an expedition to the interior to attempt to procure a specimen of the rare ember orchid. The flower is a symbol of the royal house, but all of the ember orchids in the royal hothouses have been struck by a blight and may die before the year is out.
hooks.gmNotes:
The botanist should be kind and perhaps even whimsical but decidedly committed to their charge in the Royal House and fiercely loyal to the Azcan Realm.

The expedition should lead deep into thick jungle. The botanist should need frequent protecting. Consider carnivorous plants, monkeys that attempt to make off with supplies, etc. In the end, the jungle should open onto a wide mere, with a small cluster of ember orchids growing along its edge.

But of course, there is a complication. There is a small community of gnomes living nearby who suffer from a disease which only the orchids can cure. The committed botanist will no doubt want to secure the flowers anyway, and so perhaps there will be some tension between them and Our Heroes. But there is more: The gnomes use the orchids by breathing on them, and the orchids seem to take the disease upon themselves, taking on the same appearance of blight as the orchids in the Royal House, which means... the Monarch themselves must carry this same disease, and if they don't get more orchids soon, they will die!

If you want to make the botanist more of a threat, consider having a rift among the gnomes (perhaps some want to move their community away from where they've contracted this disease), and the botanist can bribe one side of that rift to his aid (combative aid, if need be).
